data.hypothesis: Factoring the row base and advancing pointers across x should make the existing unfused stencil's unit-stride accesses clearer to the compiler's automatic vectorizer and reduce per-cell index construction. The supplied facts do not establish explicit SIMD support in the frozen build, so this candidate tests the compiler-vectorizable formulation without a SIMD pragma or ISA assumption.
data.notes: The interior x traversal still begins at x0 (normally 4); no alignment clause is used, since aligned allocation does not imply an aligned interior start. Neighbor expression order and output boundaries are preserved. The baseline was correct with mean 0.457486 seconds; this candidate has not yet been validated or measured, so no speedup is claimed.
transformations: Factor each y/z row's flattened starting address once, then advance input, velocity, and output pointers by one element for contiguous x traversal.
Preserve the stencil expression order and interior bounds; make no alignment or ISA assumptions and add no explicit SIMD directive.
